chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Awaken your heart with contemplation, and roughen your side against the night (by standing in prayer), and fear Allah, your Lord.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّفَكُّرِ: Contemplation or deep reflection on God's creation and attributes
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: The night, specifically referring to the time for night prayer (qiyam al-layl)
key_terms.جَافِ: To roughen or harden, referring to the physical discomfort endured during night prayer
key_terms.جَنْبَكَ: Your side, referring to the side of the body resting on the bed

ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual practices recommended by Imam Ali for awakening the heart and strengthening faith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits this concise directive from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), linking intellectual awakening through *tafakkur* with physical devotion in *qiyam al-layl*, a practice deeply revered in Shia piety as the time of divine proximity. This triad of contemplation, nocturnal worship, and *taqwa* reflects the Alavid emphasis on integrating inner reflection with outer discipline to achieve spiritual refinement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws was saying: ‘Awaken your heart with ‘التَّفَكُّرِ’ the contemplation, and roughen up your side at night (by standing for Salāt), and fear Allahazwj, your Lordazwj’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘Awaken your heart by thinking. Keep your side off the bed at night (meaning stand up for nightly prayers) and be pious before your Lord, Allah.’”
